pll2d9c2-d1e3514.summary: Proposes to consider what an order is and whether the orders were distinct from creation.

pll2d9c2-d1e3528.summary: Defines an order as a multitude of heavenly spirits alike in some gift of grace, as they share natural gifts. Seraphim, 'burning,' excel in charity; Cherubim, 'fullness of knowledge,' in knowledge; Thrones are so filled with grace that God sits in them and judges through them (Gregory); Dominations surpass Principalities and Powers; Principalities direct those below in divine mysteries; Powers restrain adverse powers from tempting as much as they wish; Virtues work signs and miracles; Archangels announce greater things, Angels lesser.
claims: Each order is named for a gift of grace.

pl-l2d9c2.summary: Defines an angelic order as a multitude of heavenly spirits alike in some gift of grace, as they agree in natural gifts. Seraphim burn most with charity; Cherubim excel in knowledge; Thrones are so filled with grace that God sits in them and judges through them (Gregory); Dominations surpass Principalities and Powers; Principalities direct those below them in divine mysteries; Powers restrain adverse powers from tempting as much as they wish; Virtues work signs and miracles; Archangels announce greater things, Angels lesser.
claims: An order is a multitude of spirits alike in a gift of grace.
Seraphim excel in charity, Cherubim in knowledge.
Thrones are those in whom God sits and judges.
Powers restrain demons from tempting as much as they desire.
Virtues work miracles; Archangels announce greater things, Angels lesser.
